evidence.note: Reviewed CHANGELOG.md, internal/fsm/kind/decision_test.go, internal/fsm/run/builder.go, internal/fsm/run/store_test.go and tests/go/test-git-context.sh against rubrics/task-done-review-rubric.md, adversarially, with mutation testing against a scratchpad copy of the repo (branch left untouched).

Mutation-proved TestReadRawSurfacesAMidFileReadFailure: reverting io.ReadAll to the hand-rolled break-on-error loop it replaced makes the test fail with 'a failed read was reported as success with 0 bytes'. The comment's claim about the old defect is accurate.

Mutation-proved TestSummarizeIncompleteFork: dropping the second disjunct of incompleteFork (Seq == ForkedAtSeq+1 && StateKind == KindAgentEdit) fails the 'second disjunct: one past, agent-edit' case, and narrowing the first disjunct from <= to < fails the summarize-level assertion. The test comment's claim that the second disjunct was previously unexercised now holds no longer.

Mutation-tested the new store_test.go against the code it covers: flipping the List tie-break, dropping TypeTree from countedType, changing Options.maxEvents' zero check, removing parseLines' Prev check, skipping the .gitignore re-ensure, widening the run dir mode to 0755, dropping O_NOFOLLOW, dropping TornFiles' audit.torn- prefix filter and skipping removeNeverCreated's .torn preservation each turn the package red. 15 of 16 attempted mutations across store.go, store_jsonl.go and builder.go were caught.

Verified decision_test.go's confidence table against AdjudicateThreshold = 0.7: 0.7 effective true, 0.6 and absent confidence effective false. Mutating >= to >, dropping the confidence term, defaulting absent confidence to 1.0, or extending the threshold rule to still-present all fail TestDecision. Removing either nil-judge guard in kind.go (adjudicateExec.Execute:407, stillPresentExec.Execute:580) fails TestNilJudgeExecutors.

tests/go/test-git-context.sh's lowered grep matches the actual strings at gitcontext.go:305, 319 and 327; all three copies of the message were lowercased together in the branch diff, and a repo-wide grep finds no remaining consumer of the old capitalised form outside prior review artifacts. Ran the script (exit 0) and mutated the grep pattern to a nonsense string to confirm the assertion is live (exit 1). shellcheck clean.

Spot-checked the 0.9.0 claims against the code: `metareview fsm` with no subcommand emits the exact subcommand list init|state|advance|record|gate|judge|converge|diff|export|workflows|--agent-prompt with schema_version 1 and an untrusted array, exit 2; every named flag (--from, --at-iter, --var, --allow-custom-cmds, --mock-ai, --repair, --judge-model/--judge-effort) exists in internal/fsm/cli/run.go:107-113 and prompt.go:22-40; testdata/fsm/agent-prompt.golden, commands/fsm.md, skills/fsm, docs/fsm/ and tests/go/test-fsm.sh all exist; tests/coverage.sh:88-91 does require every statement covered for internal/fsm/* and workflows; tests/run-all.sh:11-12 vets and lists the smoke-tagged judge test; MinGitVersion = 2.31 (internal/setup/setup.go:184) matches 'Requires git >= 2.31'; exports land under docs/metareview/fsm/ (export.go:122).

Checked the CHANGELOG Upgrade paragraph that reads as if it could be wrong: 'a complete but newline-less final row is kept as a row; only an undecodable fragment moves to .metareview/runs/.torn/'. It is about runs.jsonl, not the FSM audit log, and readRows (record.go:139-152) plus appendRow (record.go:216-224) implement exactly that. FSM Row.Scope is 'fsm-<workflow>' (record.go:85), so 0.8.x review-gate readers cannot match it. Not a false claim.

Verified TestOracle's comment that 'the oracle carries <>& and U+2028 in a payload': line 2's tree payload status is 'M a.go <>& x\u2028y' with the angle brackets and ampersand as literal bytes and U+2028 as an escape, so the assertion is not vacuous. The three fixtures each hold 3 lines and oracle.sha256 holds 3 hashes, so the loop guard len(want) != len(lines) cannot pass over an empty set.

go test ./... is green; go vet and golangci-lint report 0 issues on internal/fsm/run and internal/fsm/kind; internal/fsm/run reports 100.0% of statements, so every Override constructor closure in builder.go is executed at least once.

findings.note: The 'unknown kind' row in the new TestDecision table is satisfiable by two of the three wrong implementations it appears to rule out. internal/fsm/kind/decision_test.go:32 uses the payload {"match":true} -- the same payload as the 'absent field' row directly above it at line 31 -- so it can only detect an unknown kind that falls through to v.Match. Proved by mutation: rewriting internal/fsm/kind/decision.go:34-35 from `case judge.KindStillPresent: raw = v.StillPresent` to `default: raw = v.StillPresent`, so that every unrecognised kind is read as still-present, leaves `go test ./internal/fsm/...` fully green. Decision's doc comment (decision.go:16-18) explicitly promises Raw is nil 'when ... the kind is unknown', and TestDecision is the only test of kind.Decision anywhere in the module -- it feeds machine.DiffRuns from internal/fsm/cli/run.go:905, so a silently-decided unknown kind would surface as a wrong decision in `fsm diff` output. Fix by giving the unknown-kind row a payload that carries all three decision fields, e.g. {"match":true,"is_real":true,"still_present":true} with kind "other" expecting nil/nil, which then fails under any fall-through.

Dead statement in Builder.Copy. internal/fsm/run/builder.go:184 sets `child.mock = cd.Mock != ""` after the copy loop, but child.Init(cd) at builder.go:166 already performed exactly that assignment (builder.go:64) and nothing between the two touches child.mock -- the copy loop only writes child.state and child.iter. Proved by deleting line 184 in a scratchpad copy: `go test ./internal/fsm/...` stays green. Because it is a statement rather than a branch, the exactly-100% gate that tests/coverage.sh:88-91 imposes on internal/fsm/* counts it as covered while nothing asserts it, so it reads as a deliberate re-derivation that is in fact a no-op. Delete it, or if the intent was to derive mock from the copied events rather than from the child init data, say so and derive it from them.

Misleading dead parameter on Builder.stamp. internal/fsm/run/builder.go:101 declares `stamp(typ string, data any, _ []Override)` and discards the third argument. Init passes its overrides into it at builder.go:65 as though stamp applied them, then applies the same slice itself in the loop at builder.go:69-71; Event passes nil at builder.go:78 and applies them at builder.go:86-88. A reader of Init has to open stamp to learn the argument is ignored, and a future 'fix' that honours it would apply every override twice. Drop the parameter and the argument at the call site.

Builder.Copy panics rather than failing readably on the malformed logs the Override API exists to construct. internal/fsm/run/builder.go:174 indexes pb.lines[ev.Seq-1], which assumes the parent's Seq values are exactly 1..n in order, and builder.go:154 dereferences parent[0] with no length check while discarding the Unmarshal error. WithSeq (builder.go:13) is provided precisely so tests can build logs with wrong Seq values, so forking such a log gives an index-out-of-range panic that takes down the whole test binary instead of a named failure. A bounds check with a t-visible error, or a documented precondition on Copy, would keep the failure diagnosable.

Unchecked type assertion inside a test assertion path. internal/fsm/run/store_test.go:190 writes se.Cause.(*FoldError).Reason != ReasonStamp without the comma-ok form. If Append ever returns ERR_APPEND_REJECTED with a differently typed cause, the test panics on the conversion instead of printing the actual cause -- the opposite of what the storeErrE helper introduced at store_test.go:29-37 was written to achieve, and the same class of problem the file's own header comment about discarded failures is guarding against. Use the comma-ok form and t.Fatalf with se.Cause.

Weak sidecar-permission assertion in TestJSONLTornTail. The loop at internal/fsm/run/store_test.go:488-492 already identifies this iteration's sidecar by content, but the mode check at store_test.go:496 stats matches[0] -- the lexicographically first name after sort.Strings, and sidecar names are audit.torn-<nextSeq>-<nanos>.bin where nextSeq is 3 for all three iterations, so matches[0] is always the oldest sidecar. Iterations 2 and 3 therefore re-assert the 0600 mode of iteration 1's file and never check the one just written. Stat the file the loop identified instead. The comment at store_test.go:488 ('the newest sidecar carries this iteration's tail') also describes an ordering the loop does not use: it takes any sidecar whose bytes match, which happens to be sound here only because each iteration's tail string is distinct.

internal/fsm/run/builder.go is a 188-line test-fixture API (Builder, Override and eleven With* constructors, all exported) shipped in a non-test file, so it compiles into the production binary and its statements sit in the denominator of the exactly-100% gate that tests/coverage.sh:88-91 applies to internal/fsm/*. Verified there is no non-test caller anywhere in the module: every reference outside the file itself is in a _test.go. Accepted rather than blocked because cross-package tests in internal/fsm/machine legitimately need it and Go has no cross-package test-only visibility; a dedicated internal/fsm/runtest package would remove it from the shipped package and from the coverage denominator.
